sentences.text: Elornis is an extinct genus of flamingo that lived in the Late Oligocene of Ronzon, France.
Although historically classified as a member of the Phoenicopteridae, recent research suggests it may be more basal within the group.
Auguste Aymard first coined the name Elornis in 1855 during a report presented to the Congres Seientifique de France.
However, Aymard's original report only stated that the birds were flamingos without providing a full description or illustrations.
Because Aymard's original names were considered nomina nuda and his fossil material was presumed lost, Henri Milne-Edwards is credited as the authority.
Milne-Edwards described the species Elornis littoralis based on postcranial remains such as the pelvis, tarsometatarsi, tibiotarsi, and furculae.
This animal lived during the Rupelian stage, from 33.9 to 27.3 million years ago.
Research on Elornis is difficult because the current location of the fossil material is unknown, limiting data to Milne-Edwards' descriptions and illustrations.
